chitchat: Bram turns a page of the ledger and runs his pencil down a column, lips moving.
He stops on the landing, puts a hand on the rail, and gets his breath back.
"Rounded down again," he says to nobody, and makes a note.
description: A thin old man in a three-piece suit gone shiny at the knees, with a ledger under his arm and a pencil behind his ear. He takes the stairs one at a time with a hand on the rail and a pause on every landing, and he has opinions about where everything in the shop should go.

bye.text: "Mind the third step down," he says. "It's loose. It's been loose since the war."

root.text: "Mm?" He looks up from the ledger and keeps his finger on the line.

text_by_relation.familiar: "Sit down a minute," he says, "these stairs aren't getting any shorter."
text_by_relation.first:
The old man looks up from a ledger, finger on the line he was reading.

"Tolley. Bram. Fourth floor, the polished one." He taps the ledger. "Did my niece charge you right? She rounds down. Forty years I had that shop and I never once rounded down."
text_by_relation.known: "Mm. You." He goes back to the ledger. "She's moved the candles again, I suppose."

shop.text: "Forty years. It was a tobacconist when I took it, and a sweet shop, and then whatever people asked for." He shrugs. "That's all a variety store is. You keep saying yes. Effie says yes faster than I did."

clothing_layers: a brown three-piece suit shiny at the knees
a collarless shirt with a stud

name: Bram Tolley
